summary: The requirement asks for a real-time cross-currency trade settlement and clearing capability that enforces dual-authorization above $1,000,000, validates margin balance, meets a 250ms settlement latency target, degrades to a queued state on Tier-2 volatility, and emits ISO 20022 pacs.008 confirmations.

criteria.name: Independent
criteria.rationale: The requirement leans on several unstated external systems and definitions: the 'dual-authorization' workflow, the 'margin balance' calculation engine, and the 'Tier-2 thresholds' circuit-breaker classification are all referenced but never defined here, implying dependency on other requirements or systems not included.
criteria.improvement: Either inline the definitions (or link to the specific requirement/spec) for the authorization workflow, margin calculation, and Tier-2 threshold classification so this requirement can be built without waiting on undocumented external decisions.

criteria.name: Negotiable
criteria.rationale: Every bullet is a locked-in implementation detail rather than an outcome: '250ms', 'ISO 20022 compliant confirmation messages (pacs.008)', 'dual-authorization', and 'Tier-2 thresholds' prescribe exact mechanisms with no stated rationale for why these specific choices were made.
criteria.improvement: Reframe bullets around the outcome desired (e.g., 'settlements must be confirmed to counterparties quickly and in a regulator-recognized format') and move the specific numbers/protocol choices into a separate design or acceptance-criteria section that can be revisited.

criteria.name: Valuable
criteria.rationale: The opening line 'As an institutional broker, execute real-time cross-currency trade settlements with bilateral counterparty risk verification' states an action, not a benefit — there is no statement of why this matters (e.g., reduced settlement risk, regulatory compliance, capital efficiency).
criteria.improvement: Add an explicit benefit clause, e.g., 'so that counterparty exposure and settlement failure risk are minimized during high-volatility trading.'

criteria.name: Estimable
criteria.rationale: The five bullets outline distinct pieces of work (authorization gate, margin check, latency SLA, circuit-breaker state transition, message emission), giving a rough shape, but sizing is blocked by unknowns like the margin-sufficiency algorithm and the Tier-2 threshold definition.
criteria.improvement: Specify the margin calculation formula/source system and the exact Tier-2 volatility threshold values so effort can be sized without additional discovery.

criteria.name: Small
criteria.rationale: The requirement bundles five separable capabilities: dual-authorization above $1,000,000, margin balance validation, a 250ms settlement SLA, circuit-breaker-triggered queuing, and ISO 20022 pacs.008 messaging — each is independently testable and shippable work, not one coherent capability.
criteria.improvement: Split into separate requirements, e.g., 'Dual-authorization for large orders', 'Margin validation before lock-in', 'Settlement latency SLA', 'Circuit-breaker queuing behavior', and 'ISO 20022 confirmation messaging'.

criteria.name: Testable
criteria.rationale: Key statements lack observable outcomes: 'under normal market conditions' is not defined, 'sufficient margin balance' has no stated threshold or formula, and 'Tier-2 thresholds' is referenced with no numeric definition, so a tester cannot construct a pass/fail scenario for these.
criteria.improvement: Replace vague qualifiers with measurable values, e.g., define 'normal market conditions' by a volatility index range, and state the exact margin-sufficiency formula and Tier-2 threshold values.

criteria.name: Acceptance Criteria
criteria.rationale: The document is a flat bullet list of behaviors with no Given/When/Then or explicit pass/fail conditions; for example, 'Settlements must complete within 250ms under normal market conditions' has no stated measurement window, sample size, or failure handling for the case where it is exceeded.
criteria.improvement: Add an explicit acceptance-criteria section per bullet, e.g., 'Given an order under $1,000,000 and normal market volatility (index < X), when submitted, then settlement confirmation is emitted within 250ms in 99% of trades.'

criteria.name: Unambiguous
criteria.rationale: Several vague terms appear without definition: 'normal market conditions', 'sufficient margin balance', and 'Tier-2 thresholds (circuit breaker)' are all undefined qualifiers that different readers could interpret differently.
criteria.improvement: Define each vague term numerically or by reference to an authoritative source, e.g., link 'Tier-2 thresholds' to the specific circuit-breaker policy document and its numeric bands.

overall.verdict: This requirement bundles multiple large, loosely-defined capabilities with no acceptance criteria and several undefined thresholds, so it is not ready for test design until it is split up and its vague terms are quantified.

blocking_issues: No numeric definition is given for 'Tier-2 thresholds (circuit breaker)', so the queued-settlement trigger cannot be reliably tested.
No formula or data source is stated for validating 'sufficient margin balance', making that check untestable as written.
'Normal market conditions' used to scope the 250ms settlement SLA is undefined, leaving the performance requirement without a testable boundary.
The requirement bundles five distinct features (authorization, margin validation, latency SLA, circuit-breaker queuing, ISO 20022 messaging) with no acceptance criteria for any of them.
missing_information: Exact numeric definition of Tier-2 volatility thresholds that trigger the circuit breaker.
The margin-sufficiency formula or the system of record used to validate margin balance before lock-in.
Definition of 'normal market conditions' (e.g., volatility index range) that bounds the 250ms settlement SLA.
The dual-authorization workflow: who the authorizers are, how authorization is captured, and the timeout/rejection behavior.
Expected behavior and error messaging when margin balance is insufficient or dual-authorization is not obtained.
The measurement point and acceptable failure rate for the 250ms settlement SLA (e.g., percentile target, sample window).
Content/field requirements of the pacs.008 confirmation message beyond stating the message type.
